Session - Name: S08 - Reframing Cardiovascular Risk: Upstream Metabolic Drivers Across the Cardio-Kidney-Hepatic Continuum
Session - Details:
Cardiovascular disease reflects the convergence of metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and hepatic steatosis within an interconnected cardio-kidney-hepatic-metabolic (CKHM) continuum driven by obesity, insulin resistance, and systemic inflammation. For cardiologists, this evolving paradigm shifts the focus from downstream risk-factor management alone toward earlier intervention targeting shared metabolic mechanisms that accelerate atherosclerosis, heart failure progression, and renal decline.  

Cardiovascular outcomes trials have demonstrated that certain GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk populations. Emerging evidence also supports favourable effects on renal and hepatic parameters, reinforcing the concept of metabolic modulation as a strategy for multi-organ protection. Semaglutide, supported by a substantial and expanding evidence base across diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular populations, represents a significant advance within this paradigm.  

This session will examine the CKHM framework through a cardiovascular lens, review pivotal cardiovascular outcomes data alongside emerging multi-organ evidence, and discuss how upstream metabolic intervention can be integrated into contemporary cardiology practice to modify risk beyond traditional targets.

Session - Name: S08 - Reframing Cardiovascular Risk: Upstream Metabolic Drivers Across the Cardio-Kidney-Hepatic Continuum
Session - Details:
Cardiovascular disease reflects the convergence of metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and hepatic steatosis within an interconnected cardio-kidney-hepatic-metabolic (CKHM) continuum driven by obesity, insulin resistance, and systemic inflammation. For cardiologists, this evolving paradigm shifts the focus from downstream risk-factor management alone toward earlier intervention targeting shared metabolic mechanisms that accelerate atherosclerosis, heart failure progression, and renal decline.  

Cardiovascular outcomes trials have demonstrated that certain GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk populations. Emerging evidence also supports favourable effects on renal and hepatic parameters, reinforcing the concept of metabolic modulation as a strategy for multi-organ protection. Semaglutide, supported by a substantial and expanding evidence base across diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular populations, represents a significant advance within this paradigm.  

This session will examine the CKHM framework through a cardiovascular lens, review pivotal cardiovascular outcomes data alongside emerging multi-organ evidence, and discuss how upstream metabolic intervention can be integrated into contemporary cardiology practice to modify risk beyond traditional targets.
Paper Title: Reframing Cardiovascular Risk: Upstream Metabolic Drivers Across the Cardio-Kidney-Hepatic Continuum
